title: Elucidating the Suppression of High‐Voltage Degradation in O3‐type NaNi <sub>1/3</sub> Fe <sub>1/3</sub> Mn <sub>1/3</sub> O <sub>2</sub> : A Voltage‐Switching Strategy for Na‐ion Batteries
abstract: ABSTRACT Elevating depth‐of‐charge (DoC) enhances the energy density of layered oxide cathodes for sodium‐ion batteries; however, such high‐DoC cycling inevitably triggers severe structural and interfacial degradation. In practice, battery management systems commonly adapt voltage‐derating strategies dynamically according to battery state of health, achieving a favorable trade‐off between energy density and cycle life. Nevertheless, a critical yet overlooked question remains: how high‐DoC‐induced damaged regions evolve when reverted to moderate‐DoC cycling. Here, using NaNi 1/3 Fe 1/3 Mn 1/3 O 2 (NFM111) as a prototype, a voltage‐switching strategy is employed to elucidate the dynamic and long‐term behavior of these damaged regions. During high‐DoC cycling (charging to 4.3 V), the rapid capacity fading is driven by pronounced formation of bulk defects and interfacial disordered spinel phases. However, upon switching these cells to moderate‐DoC cycling (charging to 4.0 V), these pre‐existing damaged regions become stabilized: their rapid propagation is suppressed, and they no longer accelerate degradation in surrounding intact regions. This enables degraded NFM111 to deliver capacity retention comparable to that of cells cycled solely under moderate‐DoC conditions. This work presents a dynamic and evolving picture of high‐DoC degradation and subsequent moderate‐DoC stabilization in NFM111 cathodes, providing mechanistic insights into voltage‐derating process and the lifetime prolongation of compromised cells.

title: A Hybrid VMD–GWO–BiLSTM–Attention Framework for Accurate State-of-Health Prediction of Lithium-Ion Batteries Under Complex Degradation Dynamics
abstract: Accurate State-of-Health (SOH) prediction for lithium-ion batteries is essential for the safe and stable operation of Battery Management Systems (BMSs). However, achieving high-precision estimation remains challenging due to the complex interplay of non-stationary degradation characteristics, observation noise, and bidirectional temporal dependencies. This study proposes a robust hybrid temporal prediction framework integrating Variational Mode Decomposition (VMD), Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory (BiLSTM) networks, an Attention mechanism, and the Grey Wolf Optimizer (GWO). First, VMD is employed to decompose the raw SOH time-series signals, isolating observation noise and mitigating temporal non-stationarity. A BiLSTM network is then utilized to extract bidirectional temporal correlations throughout the aging process, while an attention mechanism adaptively allocates weights to focus on critical degradation features. Furthermore, GWO automatically searches for optimal network hyperparameters, eliminating the subjective bias of manual tuning and enhancing cross-condition generalization. The proposed framework is rigorously validated using full-lifecycle datasets of four lithium-ion batteries (CS2_35 to CS2_38) from the CALCE laboratory. Standard temporal networks (LSTM, GRU, and Transformer) serve as comparative baselines, alongside an intra-battery ablation study to quantify the performance gain of each module. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed VMD–GWO–BiLSTM–Attention framework achieves enhanced prediction accuracy compared to standard baseline temporal models (LSTM, GRU, and Transformer) across all evaluated degradation profiles. For the CS2_35 battery with a smooth aging trend, the root mean square error (RMSE) and mean absolute percentage error (MAPE) are minimized to 0.008 and 1.442%, respectively. Even under the severe capacity fluctuations of the CS2_38 battery, the model successfully controls the RMSE at 0.012 and the MAPE at 2.541%, exhibiting a significant error reduction compared to all baselines. These findings confirm that the synergistic integration of these four modules effectively addresses complex, nonlinear battery aging scenarios, offering a viable methodological baseline for deep-learning-based SOH prediction.
title_zh: A Hybrid VMD–GWO–BiLSTM–Attention Framework for Accurate State-of-Health Prediction of Lithium-Ion Batteries Under Complex Degradation Dynamics
